transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been avoiding a lot of things. Anything that reminds me of my old job—office buildings, security talks, even networking events near work sites. And if people start asking about the day it happened, I usually make an excuse and leave.
Can you tell me more about what happened at your job that’s been bothering you?

It was… a confrontation at work. I don’t really like going into it.

I remember seeing the gun, and after that there’s just this blank spot. I can tell you all the mistakes they said I made afterward, every one of those, but that part right after I saw it… I can’t piece it together. It just isn’t there.
Since the incident, have you had any recurring thoughts, nightmares, or flashbacks where you feel like you’re reliving the moment you saw the gun?

Yeah… sometimes. It’ll just come out of nowhere. I can be doing dishes, or driving past a warehouse gate, and it’s like that scene snaps back into my head. I can hear people panicking, and my chest gets tight… like I’m right back there for a second.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of avoidance, intrusive recollections, and sudden flashbacks following a traumatic workplace incident align with PTSD. Other candidates (F40.00, F40.11, F32.0) are less consistent given the absence of primary phobic, panic-related, or major depressive features.

candidates: F32.0 - Major depressive disorder, mild episode
